title: Hostname/mailbox corpus tests use Rfc5280Profile, not the profile rustdoc recommends
description: pkix-chain/tests/hostname_corpus.rs uses `Rfc5280Profile` for verify_tls_server tests. pkix-chain/src/lib.rs:720 rustdoc says 'typically BasicTlsProfile or WebPkiProfile' which would REQUIRE id-kp-serverAuth. Rfc5280Profile is permissive — no EKU enforcement. The corpus tests therefore validate the SAN-binding mechanics but DO NOT verify that a non-serverAuth cert (e.g., a code-signing cert that happens to carry a DNS SAN) is correctly rejected. This is a coverage gap: a caller using BasicTlsProfile with verify_tls_server expects 'TLS server' semantics, but the test suite never confirms that the wrapper enforces the EKU. Fix: parallel run of one or two corpus cases under BasicTlsProfile, with a fixture that has a DNS SAN but lacks id-kp-serverAuth. Confirms the EKU enforcement composes with SAN matching. (Note: test case #25 'basictls_profile_exact_match' uses BasicTls but only on a cert that has the correct EKU — does not exercise the rejection path.)
close_reason:
Fixed, as the bead specified. Added basictls_profile_rejects_a_matching_san_without_serverauth to pkix-chain/tests/hostname_corpus.rs, with the fixture it asked for.

The bead was right about the gap, and right that it needed a new fixture. The corpus drives Rfc5280Profile (no EKU enforcement), and the single existing BasicTlsProfile case -- basictls_profile_exact_match -- is positive-only. A fixture that satisfies every check cannot tell "profile applied" apart from "profile ignored", so that test would pass with EKU enforcement entirely absent. Nothing confirmed the composition.

Fixture: host-exact-foo-codesigning-eku.der, added to gen.py. Same SAN as host-exact-foo.der (DNS foo.example.com) and checked against the same target, so the SAN requirement is satisfied and identity binding succeeds; EKU is codeSigning rather than serverAuth. The rejection is therefore attributable to the EKU alone.

Why a new fixture was unavoidable: the three existing non-serverAuth leaves (leaf-codesigning.der, leaf-timestamping.der, leaf-ocsp-responder.der) carry NO SAN. Under BasicTlsProfile each fails require_subject_alt_name first, so a rejection proves nothing about EKU enforcement. Confirmed with openssl before concluding this.

The test also runs the same certificate and target under Rfc5280Profile and requires Ok, so a bad fixture surfaces as a failed control rather than a passing assertion.

Verified by mutation: setting BasicTlsProfile required_leaf_eku = None makes it fail with "a codeSigning leaf with a matching DNS SAN must still be rejected, but it was accepted". Note the naive mutation does not compile -- ID_KP_SERVER_AUTH becomes unused and -D warnings rejects it -- so the constant has to be kept referenced.

Cost worth recording: all 38 fixtures were rewritten. gen.py calls ec.generate_private_key per run and never persists the root key, so there is no way to sign one new leaf under the existing root; any addition re-signs everything. The fixtures README documents regeneration as the workflow, nothing pins fixture bytes or serials, and the full suite passes on the regenerated set. If fixture additions become common, seeding the root key deterministically would remove that churn.

Gates green: fmt, clippy, rustdoc, 2346 tests.
